subject: storytime
title: The Tortoise and the Hare
about: Aesop's fable of the boastful hare who stops for a nap and the slow tortoise who keeps going and wins the race. Fables are the first read-aloud domain of the NC/CKLA Grade 1 year (Fables and Stories), and this one gives him a line he will hear for the rest of his life: slow and steady wins the race. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, three pages long.
tip: Act it out: you be the hare and take a nap while he plods past you saying step, step, step.

book.author: Aesop (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A race between the fastest and the slowest.

passage.text:
A hare liked to run fast.
He liked to brag, too.
"I am the fastest of all!" he said.
A tortoise was slow.
He walked step by step.
"Let's have a race," said the tortoise.
The hare laughed and laughed.
"You want to race me?"
"Yes, let's race!"
***
A fox said, "Ready, set, go!"
The hare ran off like the wind.
The tortoise plodded along.
Step, step, step.
Soon the hare was far ahead.
He looked back.
He could not see the tortoise at all.
"I have lots of time," said the hare.
"I will take a little nap."
He lay down under a tree.
Soon he was fast asleep.
***
The tortoise did not stop.
Step, step, step.
He went past the sleeping hare.
Step, step, step.
He got close to the finish line.
The hare woke up.
He saw the tortoise at the line!
He ran as fast as he could.
But it was too late.
The tortoise won the race!
"Slow and steady wins the race," said the fox.

cards.q: Who liked to brag about being fast?
cards.note: A hare is a big rabbit with long legs, built for speed.
The fox starts the race and says the lesson at the end.

cards.q: What did the hare do under the tree?
cards.note: He was so sure he would win that he stopped trying.

cards.q: How did the tortoise move in the race?
cards.note: Slow, but he never stopped; that is what steady means.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: The bragging comes before the race even starts.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: The hare woke up too late to catch him.

cards.q: How did the hare feel when he saw the tortoise at the line?
cards.note: He thought the race was his, so seeing the tortoise there was a shock.
Keep going and do not quit, even if you are not the fastest.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'plodded' mean?
cards.note: To plod is to walk slowly with heavy steps; plod across the room together.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
